headline: Brazilian industry groups criticize central bank's decision to hold Selic rate
summary: Industry and commerce entities in Brazil have criticized the Central Bank's decision to maintain the Selic interest rate at 13.75%, citing negative impacts on economic activity, credit, and public investment.
why: The Selic rate is Brazil's primary tool for controlling inflation; high rates increase borrowing costs for businesses and consumers, often slowing economic growth.

impacts.name: Brazil
impacts.why: High interest rates generally dampen economic activity and increase the cost of capital.
